item.title: Lighthouse Gold issues 35 million shares to option a Guyana gold property
item.description: The CSE has accepted the property option deal for filing, though transfer of Guyana's mining permits still needs approval from the country's mines regulator.
item.content:encoded: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT), a Canadian gold explorer focused on Guyana, said it has received acceptance from the Canadian Securities Exchange for its acquisition of the Mariwa–Sardine Hill–Lower Cuyuni gold property in the Oko Gold District of Guyana's Cuyuni-Mazaruni region. The deal is a definitive property option purchase agreement with the vendor, 1464911 B.C. Ltd. Lighthouse Gold has now paid US$150,000 cash and issued 35,000,000 common shares at a deemed C$0.185 each, worth C$6,475,000, on top of a US$100,000 deposit paid earlier under the original letter of intent. The release describes this as an option rather than an outright purchase: Lighthouse Gold 'holds the exclusive right to acquire a 100% interest' in the property, and the company says any transfer of the underlying mining permits on exercise of that option is subject to approval from Guyana's Geology and Mines Commission. The vendor, 1464911 B.C. Ltd., already held 20,000 Lighthouse Gold shares before the deal and now holds 35,020,000, about 15.99% of the company, following what Lighthouse Gold describes as an arm's-length transaction. The underlying property, Mariwa–Sardine Hill – Lower Cuyuni, sits in the Oko Gold District of Guyana's Cuyuni-Mazaruni region and comprises three medium-scale mining permits covering about 3,240 acres. Each permit was originally granted on November 4, 2015 for a five-year term and has since been renewed by the Guyana Geology and Mines Commission; the release states the permits are currently in good standing. Lighthouse Gold describes the property as being at an early exploration stage, with no established mineral resources or reserves. The 35,000,000 consideration shares are subject to a resale restriction until the later of four months and one day from issuance, or ten trading days after the company files financial statements reflecting the acquisition's value. Today's announcement follows two earlier releases on the same transaction, dated June 15 and October 20, 2026, as the deal progressed toward the CSE's acceptance for filing. Separately, Lighthouse Gold said a private placement it announced on October 22 and October 23, 2026, has been terminated. No securities were issued and no proceeds were received under that financing, and the release gives no reason for the termination and discloses no replacement financing plan. Lighthouse Gold describes itself as a Canadian gold exploration company focused on advancing exploration and mining assets in Guyana. The release names Will Rascan as interim chief executive officer and Geoff Balderson as chief financial officer and a director, and states that the Canadian Securities Exchange and its Regulation Services Provider do not accept responsibility for the release's adequacy or accuracy.

item.title: 600,000 Nvidia AI chips sit stranded in Hong Kong as China withholds approval
item.description: Beijing has let only small allotments of about 10,000 H200 chips reach each of four major Chinese tech firms, even as unofficial prices for the chips in China triple.
item.content:encoded: About 600,000 of Nvidia's advanced H200 artificial-intelligence chips are sitting in warehouses in Hong Kong awaiting shipment into mainland China, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters, as Beijing withholds approval for large-scale imports despite strong demand from Chinese technology firms. Major Chinese internet companies — Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek and Tencent among them — have each received only about 10,000 H200 chips in recent months, the people said, with additional small quantities reaching the mainland through intermediaries and indirect routes. US export controls dating to 2022 had previously restricted China's access to Nvidia's most capable AI accelerators, and Beijing has imposed its own constraints on the imports in turn, reflecting concern about dependence on American technology. Earlier reporting cited by Reuters said Beijing had told companies in July that they could expect approval for fewer than 200,000 H200 chips in total for training AI models, with priority for everyday inference work going to domestically made processors instead. China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the National Development and Reform Commission did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment, nor did Nvidia or the four technology companies named in the report. The scarcity has pushed unofficial prices sharply higher inside China. An eight-card H200 server was offered for more than 6 million yuan, or about $900,000, in the mainland market by late October — roughly three times its price a year earlier, Reuters reported. Servers built around Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips were commanding more than 20 million yuan apiece in the same unofficial market. On the TSX Venture and CSE boards, 29 listed venture names make up this bulletin's artificial-intelligence theme. Seventeen of them traded today: four moved higher and five moved lower, for a median move of +0.00% against a +2.48% gain for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Twelve saw no trades at all. Four of the theme's names were among the largest movers. Rocket Doctor AI Inc. (CSE: AIDR), whose registered name contains "ai," rose 6.45% to C$0.495. Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI), also qualifying on its name, fell 3.43% to C$1.97. GoGo AI Network Inc. (CSE: GOGO) and Perimeter Medical Imaging Ai In (TSXV: PINK), both in the theme for the same reason, were unchanged at C$0.015 and C$0.18 respectively. The moves and the Hong Kong stockpile report fall on the same trading day. Nothing in Reuters' reporting, or in the companies' own filings, connects the two. Twelve of the theme's 29 listed names did not trade at all today.

item.title: Copper One's 19.9 million special warrants convert into shares and warrants
item.description: The automatic conversion, completing a September financing, hands holders new common shares plus warrants exercisable at $0.50 for two years.
item.content:encoded: Copper One Resources Corp. (CSE: CEXY; OTC: CEXYF; FSE: IW8) will see 19,889,750 special warrants, issued September 29, 2026, automatically convert into common shares and warrants on November 6, 2026, the company said. The special warrants were issued in two tranches: 12,383,000 non-flow-through special warrants and 7,506,750 flow-through special warrants. Holders do not need to take any action; the conversion happens automatically under the terms of the original offering. The conversion delivers a combined 19,889,750 common shares along with 9,944,875 share purchase warrants to the former special warrant holders. Each warrant entitles the holder to buy one common share at $0.50 for two years from the offering's closing date. The company may accelerate that two-year expiry on 30 days' notice if Copper One's shares trade at $1.25 or higher for five consecutive trading days on the Canadian Securities Exchange. A prospectus supplement dated November 3, 2026 was filed to qualify the distribution of the securities underlying the special warrants in British Columbia, Alberta and Ontario, and is available on SEDAR+. It follows a short form base shelf prospectus the company filed in May 2025, as amended in March and October 2026. Copper One trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange under CEXY, on the US over-the-counter market under CEXYF, and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under IW8. This release does not restate the price or use of proceeds from the original special warrant offering; it covers only the terms of today's automatic conversion and the prospectus supplement that qualifies the resulting shares and warrants for distribution.

item.title: CopperCorp plans to raise up to C$3 million and shrink its share count
item.description: The explorer's non-brokered placement pairs units and subscription receipts with a one-for-five share consolidation ahead of TSX Venture Exchange approval.
item.content:encoded: CopperCorp Resources Inc. (TSXV: CPER; OTCQB: CPCPF), which is exploring for copper, gold and rare earth elements at its AMC project in western Tasmania, Australia, intends to raise up to C$3.0 million through a non-brokered private placement, the company said. The offering's first tranche is up to 4,444,444 units priced at $0.1125 each, for gross proceeds of up to $500,000. Each unit is made up of one post-consolidation common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.18 for 24 months from the date of issue. The second tranche is up to 18,518,519 subscription receipts priced at $0.135 each, for gross proceeds of up to $2.5 million. Once escrow release conditions are satisfied, each receipt converts into a unit comprising one post-consolidation common share and one-half of a warrant, exercisable at $0.24 for 24 months. The conversion is contingent on completion of the sale of the company's Skyline Project, among other escrow conditions. CopperCorp is also proceeding with a share consolidation on a one-for-five basis, reducing its roughly 118.96 million shares outstanding to approximately 23.79 million. Securities issued in the placement will be subject to the usual four-month-and-one-day resale hold. Company insiders may participate, which the company says will be treated as related-party transactions. Proceeds are earmarked for exploration and drilling at the AMC project and for general corporate and working capital purposes, the company said. The offering and the share consolidation both remain subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, and finder's fees may be paid to eligible arm's-length parties under the exchange's policies. CopperCorp also trades on the OTCQB market in the United States under the symbol CPCPF.

item.title: Ukrainian drones set fire to a major Ozon warehouse in Russia
item.description: The attack hit Adygeysk for a second time, even as Ozon had already projected $367 million in losses from strikes on 11 of its sites.
item.content:encoded: A Ukrainian drone strike set fire to a logistics hub operated by Russian e-commerce retailer Ozon in Adygeysk, in southern Russia, on November 4, 2026, the company and a regional official said. It was the second time this specific facility had been hit. Debris from the strike also damaged two nearby villages, according to reporting on the attack. Ozon said it was not aware of any casualties and that all staff at the site had been evacuated. The strike is part of a broader Ukrainian campaign that has targeted dozens of warehouses run by Ozon and its rival Wildberries since July, aimed at disrupting Russia's economy and its war effort, according to reporting on the pattern of attacks. Ozon said it would cancel orders it could not fulfil from the Adygeysk site and would temporarily stop accepting deliveries from third-party sellers there while it assesses the damage. Ahead of this strike, Ozon had already projected 30.1 billion roubles (about $367 million) in losses from drone attacks across 11 of its sites, the company said in a financial results release last week. Ozon's stock fell about 0.4% following the latest attack. The strike came as both sides prepared for peace talks scheduled for November 10 and 11, and followed a Ukrainian strike on a Russian oil refinery and Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure in the preceding days. On Canada's venture boards, the defence and drones theme comprises eight listed names. Six traded today, two higher and four lower, for a median move of -2.62% against +2.48% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of -5.10 percentage points. The attack on Ozon's logistics hub and these moves fall on the same trading day; nothing in either release ties one to the other. Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp (CSE: QESS) rose 5.66% to C$0.28 and is in the theme because its registered name contains "defence." Kraken Robotics Inc (TSXV: PNG) fell 5.57% to C$3.56 and is in the theme because its registered name is Kraken Robotics Inc. Both traded today; the group's median move was negative even though these two names moved in opposite directions.

item.title: Midterm results lift hopes for an end to 50% aluminum tariffs
item.description: Canadian producers have already rerouted roughly 800,000 tonnes of shipments to Europe as Washington's 50 per cent tariff reshapes trade flows.
item.content:encoded: Canada's aluminum industry is watching the outcome of the U.S. midterm elections for a sign that Washington might ease the 50 per cent tariff it has placed on Canadian aluminum exports. Jean Simard, chief executive of the Aluminum Association of Canada, said he is 'far more optimistic than I've ever been, because the signal is overwhelmingly clearer than I thought it would be.' The 50 per cent rate has been in place since June 4, 2025, when Washington doubled an earlier 25 per cent tariff that took effect in March 2025. Tariffs on Canadian aluminum go back further still: a 10 per cent duty was first imposed in 2018. Three producers account for most of the Canadian industry's primary output: Rio Tinto, Alcoa and Aluminerie Alouette. Faced with the tariff, Canadian producers have redirected shipments toward Europe. Exports there have totalled roughly 800,000 tonnes since March 2025, against about 100,000 tonnes over a comparable period under normal market conditions. Canada produces about 3.3 million tonnes of aluminum annually and has historically sent about 90 per cent of it to the United States. Andreas Schotter of Western University cautioned against reading the midterm results as a clean signal that U.S. trade policy will soften, saying 'even on the Democratic side, there's a strong "America First" notion.' The Canadian Federation of Independent Business has reported that 87 per cent of Canadian small businesses want a tariff agreement reached as quickly as possible. None of the venture names in CM Bulletin's tariffs theme traded enough today to clear the C$25,000 daily-volume floor the theme is measured against, so this entry names none of them. That is itself a fact about the theme worth recording: whatever exposure the junior board carries to a resolution of the aluminum dispute, it was not visible in today's trading. Nothing in this report ties the midterm results to any specific change in U.S. trade policy; Simard's optimism is his own reading of the political signal, not a description of an announced decision.

item.title: AMD discloses a $2.9-billion price for AI chipmaker Taalas
item.description: The Toronto startup, founded three years ago by former AMD executives, was valued at just over $750 million last November.
item.content:encoded: AMD disclosed in a securities filing that it will pay approximately US$2.9 billion, in cash and stock, for Taalas, the Toronto-based chipmaker it first agreed to acquire in August. The filing states that US$1.4 billion of the total purchase amount is dependent on unspecified conditions, which the filing did not detail. The acquisition has not yet closed and remains subject to regulatory approval. Taalas designs semiconductor chips built for a single purpose: running the inference step of large language models, rather than the general-purpose processors AMD and its rivals have historically built. Its first chip was tailored specifically to Meta Platforms' Llama family of models, a narrower design approach than the flexible chips most of the industry produces. The company was founded in August 2023 by Ljubisa Bajic, who serves as chief executive, along with Lejla Bajic and Drago Ignjatovic. All three are former long-time AMD executives, placing the deal inside a small circle of engineers who previously worked for the acquirer. Taalas had raised more than US$225 million in venture financing before the AMD deal, including a US$169 million Series B round closed in February with investors including Fidelity and Quiet Capital. In November 2025 the company issued equity at US$94.51 a share, implying a valuation above US$750 million at the time — a figure the US$2.9-billion price represents a sharp markup on. On the venture boards, AMD's filing coincided with no broad move in the companies in CM Bulletin's artificial intelligence theme. Of 29 listed venture names carrying 'ai' in their registered names, 18 traded today — 5 higher and 5 lower — for a median move of +0.00%, against a +2.48% gain for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of 2.48 percentage points. The largest move in the theme was Datametrex AI Limited (TSXV: DM), which rose 125.00% to C$0.045. Rocket Doctor AI Inc. (CSE: AIDR) rose 6.45% to C$0.495. Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) fell 3.43% to C$1.97. GoGo AI Network Inc. (CSE: GOGO) and Perimeter Medical Imaging Ai Inc. (TSXV: PINK) were both unchanged, at C$0.015 and C$0.18 respectively. Nothing ties any of these moves to AMD's disclosure; they fell on the same day and nothing more. AMD has not disclosed when the Taalas deal is expected to close, beyond saying it remains subject to regulatory approval.

item.title: North Korea tests new air-defence missile in its fourth launch this month
item.description: State media said a cruise missile unit also struck a virtual airport target in a drill from the east coast.
item.content:encoded: North Korea said it test-fired a newly designed air-defence missile system, according to state media KCNA. The agency said North Korea separately staged a cruise-missile strike drill the same day, carried out by a sub-unit of its long-range strategic cruise missile unit. The cruise-missile drill struck a virtual airport target and was staged from the Sondok area on North Korea's east coast, KCNA said. KCNA said the air-defence test confirmed the 'technical specifications and reliability' of new materials and multiple guidance modes used in the missile, as well as the system's ability to identify and track targets. South Korea's Defence Ministry separately confirmed that Pyongyang had fired multiple missiles toward the sea from the Sondok area. Reuters reported that the exercises marked the fourth North Korean weapons launch in a month. On the venture boards, CM Bulletin's defence-and-drones theme comprises eight listed venture names. Six traded today, two higher and four lower, for a median move of -2.62 per cent, against a +2.48 per cent gain for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 5.10 percentage points between the theme and the board. Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE: QESS), which is in the theme because its registered name contains 'defence,' rose 5.66 per cent to C$0.28. Kraken Robotics Inc. (TSXV: PNG), named for being Kraken Robotics Inc., fell 5.57 per cent to C$3.56. Both moves fell on the same day as North Korea's test; neither is connected to it. Nothing connects North Korea's test to trading in CM Bulletin's defence-and-drones theme. The two fall on the same day in different markets, and no figure in this report should be read as evidence that one moved the other.

item.title: Bastion Square Partners II raises $1.5 million in its TSX Venture debut
item.description: The Vancouver capital pool company sold 15 million shares at 10 cents each and will look for an acquisition target to complete its qualifying transaction.
item.content:encoded: Bastion Square Partners II Inc., a Vancouver-based capital pool company, closed its initial public offering on November 3, 2026, raising $1.5 million in gross proceeds through the sale of 15,000,000 common shares at $0.10 each. The TSX Venture Exchange approved the listing on November 2, and the shares began trading under a halt pending closing. Trading in the shares, under the symbol BASQ.P, is scheduled to resume on November 9, 2026. Following the offering, the company has 27,000,000 common shares outstanding, of which 13,825,000 are held in escrow. Independent Trading Group (ITG), Inc. acted as agent for the offering. It received a cash commission of $55,000, a corporate finance fee of $10,000, reimbursement of its legal fees and expenses, and 500,000 non-transferable warrants exercisable at $0.10 per share until November 3, 2028. The company's directors and officers were granted 2,700,000 incentive stock options at an exercise price of $0.10, exercisable for five years. Directors also personally purchased 1,825,000 of the shares sold in the offering, a related-party transaction disclosed in the filing. A capital pool company such as Bastion Square has no business or assets of its own beyond the cash raised at listing. Under TSX Venture Exchange rules, it must use the proceeds to identify and evaluate a business or asset to acquire, a process the exchange calls a qualifying transaction. The release named Briony Bayer, the company's Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, as the contact for further information. It did not disclose any potential acquisition target or sector of interest.

item.title: Global Uranium raises its private placement minimum and adds a $1 million loan
item.description: The Calgary-based explorer increased the minimum subscription to $800,000 and secured a separate credit facility to fund its Saskatchewan and Wyoming uranium projects.
item.content:encoded: Global Uranium Corp. (CSE: GURN; OTCQB: GURFF) filed an amended and restated offering document on November 3, 2026 for its non-brokered private placement under the listed issuer financing exemption (LIFE). The minimum subscription was increased to 3,636,364 units for gross proceeds of $800,000.08; the maximum offering remains 4,239,711 units for $932,736.42, both at an unchanged price of $0.22 per unit. Each unit comprises one common share and one warrant exercisable at $0.30 per share. The warrant does not become exercisable until 61 days after closing and expires 24 months after closing. Closing is expected on or about November 6, 2026, subject to regulatory approvals including those of the Canadian Securities Exchange. The release said the securities are expected to be immediately freely tradable under applicable Canadian securities laws, subject to the restrictions that apply to control persons, and that the offering is available to purchasers in Canada other than Quebec and New Brunswick. Separately, the Calgary-based uranium explorer entered a committed, unsecured, non-revolving loan facility of up to $1,000,000 with an arm's-length lender. Advances can be requested on five business days' notice until October 30, 2028, each carrying 12% simple annual interest and due for repayment 24 months after it is drawn, with all amounts owed no later than November 3, 2030. No funds had been drawn as of the announcement. The facility carries no demand-repayment clause and allows prepayment without penalty, the company said. Proceeds from both the placement and the facility are earmarked for exploration expenditures and option payments on the company's Astro uranium project in Saskatchewan and its Wyoming projects in the Great Divide Basin, Gas Hills and Copper Mountain districts, as well as corporate liabilities, administration and working capital. The release does not name the arm's-length lender, and does not name an agent for the private placement.

item.title: AMD takes a $1.07 billion charge tied to its OpenAI and Meta chip deals
item.description: The non-cash charge reflects warrants that let the two AI customers buy up to roughly 10% of the chipmaker.
item.content:encoded: Advanced Micro Devices recorded a $1.07 billion non-cash charge, equal to 66 cents a share, in the third quarter ended September 26. The charge relates to warrants the chipmaker has issued to OpenAI and Meta Platforms as part of multibillion-dollar agreements to supply them with AI chips. Under a February agreement, AMD agreed to sell Meta up to $60 billion of AI chips over five years. Meta received warrants allowing it to buy as much as 10% of AMD if certain shipment milestones are met. AMD shares rose 8% in extended trading after the results, and the company forecast 2027 growth faster than previously expected. Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, said of the broader trend of chipmakers issuing customer warrants: "While I do believe incentives played a role in some of their sales, I believe the bigger issue is that there is pent-up demand for a serious alternative to Nvidia." AMD is not alone in using warrants to secure large AI customers. Cerebras has granted OpenAI warrants against a $20 billion commitment, Marvell issued Google warrants for a potential $12.2 billion stake, and Qualcomm gave Amazon warrants as part of a $60 billion deal, according to the report. On Canada's venture boards, the artificial intelligence and data-centre theme comprises 29 listed names; 16 traded today, 6 higher and 5 lower, for a median move of +0.00% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of 0.77 percentage points in the theme's favour. Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) rose 0.99% to CAD2.04, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai". Predictiv AI Inc. (CSE: PAI) was unchanged at CAD0.105, also because its registered name contains "ai", as was Yocale.ai Inc. (CSE: YAI), unchanged at CAD0.74. Roughly $55,000 of Sparc AI shares changed hands on the day, versus about $29,000 for Predictiv AI and $54,000 for Yocale.ai. item.title: Saudi Aramco's profit jumps 34% to $36.25 billion despite attacks on its facilities
item.description: Elevated crude and product prices drove the profit rise, and the board authorized a $21.9 billion dividend, even as Houthi strikes hit its facilities and Iranian activity disrupted Hormuz shipping.
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabian Oil Co. reported third-quarter net profit of $36.25 billion, up 34% from a year earlier, as revenue climbed to $140.5 billion from $111.6 billion over the same period. The company attributed the increase to higher prices for crude oil and refined chemical products, even as sales volumes fell. The results followed attacks on Aramco's operations: Houthi militants from Yemen launched missile and drone strikes targeting company facilities, including its Dhahran headquarters and refining operations in Jazan and Riyadh, while Iranian activity in the Strait of Hormuz disrupted shipping. Chief executive Amin Nasser said: "Geopolitical uncertainty and attacks on key energy facilities continued to amplify the global energy supply crisis in the third quarter of 2026." Aramco's board authorized a base dividend of $21.9 billion for the third quarter, up 3.5% from a year earlier and payable in the fourth quarter of 2026. Capital expenditure for the quarter totaled $10.5 billion, down from $12.6 billion a year earlier, and the company said it is pursuing additional overseas storage capacity and alternative export routes to help maintain supply reliability amid the disruptions. On Canada's venture boards, the oil, gas and power theme comprises 72 listed venture names; 34 traded today, 12 higher and 11 lower, for a median move of +0.00% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of 0.77 percentage points. The largest mover was Stamper Oil And Gas Corp (TSXV: STMP), up 40.00% to CAD0.14, followed by Reconnaissance Energy Africa Lt (TSXV: RECO), up 4.00% to CAD0.52; both are in the theme because their sector label is "Oil & Gas E&P". Among the decliners, Coelacanth Energy Inc (TSXV: CEI) fell 2.90% to CAD0.67, Lotus Creek Exploration Inc (TSXV: LTC) fell 1.77% to CAD4.43, and Robinson Energy Limited (TSXV: ROB) fell 1.52% to CAD3.24, each for the same reason. Aramco's results and the moves among these five Canadian oil and gas names fell on the same calendar day. Nothing in either the company's release or the venture names' trading establishes a connection between the two, and none is drawn here.

item.title: New Break closes $523,820 flow-through financing for its Timmins-area gold project
item.description: The CSE-listed junior issued 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 each to fund drilling at its Moray gold project near Timmins, Ontario.
item.content:encoded: New Break Resources Ltd. has closed a non-brokered private placement of 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of $523,820, the company said. The shares qualify as "flow-through shares" under the Income Tax Act, and the proceeds will be used for Canadian exploration expenses, which qualify as flow-through mining expenditures under the same legislation. The proceeds will fund continued drilling at the company's Moray gold project, located approximately 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, New Break said. The company will renounce the Canadian exploration expenses to the purchasers of the flow-through shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The financing closed November 3, 2026, and remains subject to final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange. New Break paid $12,012 in finder's fees in connection with the closing and issued 54,600 finder warrants, each exercisable into one common share at a price of $0.22 for a period of 24 months, the company said. The flow-through shares themselves carry no warrants and are subject to a hold period expiring March 4, 2027. Patricia Quigley, described in the release as a "control person" of the company, purchased 455,000 of the flow-through shares in the offering. New Break said the issuance constitutes a related-party transaction under applicable securities rules, but qualifies for an exemption from the formal valuation and minority-approval requirements because it does not exceed 25 per cent of the company's market capitalization.

item.title: Organigram offers $561 million to beat Curaleaf's hostile bid for Aurora Cannabis
item.description: The $7.80-a-share offer, payable in cash, stock or a mix of both, tops Curaleaf Holdings' hostile US$5 bid by about 21 per cent.
item.content:encoded: Organigram Global Inc. has agreed to acquire Aurora Cannabis Inc. in a transaction the companies valued at approximately $561 million, offering Aurora shareholders $7.80 per share. The offer follows several months in which Aurora had been fending off a hostile takeover attempt from Curaleaf Holdings Inc., based in Stamford, Connecticut, according to the companies. Aurora shareholders will be able to elect one of three forms of consideration: cash only, 5.86 Organigram shares for each Aurora share, or a combination of $3.75 in cash and 3.04 Organigram shares. Organigram's offer represents a roughly 21-per-cent premium to Curaleaf's latest bid of US$5 a share, the companies said. The transaction requires approval from at least two-thirds of the votes cast by Aurora shareholders at a special meeting expected to take place in December for the deal to proceed, the companies said. Organigram is funding the acquisition through a $188-million private placement with British American Tobacco and $210 million in loan facilities from ATB Financial, the companies said. If the deal receives shareholder approval, the combined company would operate five EU-GMP certified facilities. On the venture boards, the cannabis theme comprises eight listed venture names. Two traded today, none higher and one lower, for a median move of -2.17 per cent against -0.77 per cent for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of -1.40 percentage points between the theme and the broader venture board. Decibel Cannabis Company Inc. (TSXV: DB) was unchanged at C$1.80, and is included in the theme because its registered name contains "cannabis." The move falls on the same trading day as the Organigram-Aurora announcement; nothing in the day's trading data establishes a connection between the two.

item.title: PyroGenesis pays $3.1 million for its Montreal plant after a legal fight
item.description: The TSX-listed company had sued the building's owner to enforce its option to buy the Turcot facility before settling the case in May.
item.content:encoded: PyroGenesis Inc. has completed its purchase of the Turcot manufacturing facility, a roughly 40,902-square-foot (3,800-square-metre) property at 5655 Philippe-Turcot in Montreal, Quebec, the company said. PyroGenesis has occupied the building, located about 6.2 kilometres from its downtown Montreal headquarters, since September 1, 2012, and plans to remain there under a lease agreement following completion of the purchase. The purchase follows a legal dispute in which PyroGenesis filed an action in the Superior Court of Quebec seeking an order requiring the facility's owner to convey title under the company's existing contractual option to purchase, which the owner had contested. The parties reached a binding settlement in May 2026 that concluded the legal proceedings, with PyroGenesis prevailing in its right to acquire the property, the company said. The purchase price was $3.1 million, PyroGenesis said. The company is now in discussions with interested parties regarding a sale-leaseback of the property, which it said would "unlock the building's value while maintaining operations at this strategic location," and said it intends to pursue the sale-leaseback "at our own pace." PyroGenesis describes itself as a leader in ultra-high-temperature plasma processes and a technology provider to heavy industry and the defence sector, according to the release. The company said proceeds from any eventual sale-leaseback would help "accelerate projects across its various business segments," without specifying which.

item.title: Pantera Silver's shares resume trading after its cease-trade order was lifted
item.description: The TSX Venture Exchange reinstated trading Thursday after Pantera filed financial statements and the B.C. Securities Commission revoked the order.
item.content:encoded: The TSX Venture Exchange has reinstated trading in Pantera Silver Corp.'s common shares after a cease trade order imposed by the British Columbia Securities Commission, the company said. Trading is set to resume at market open on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Pantera's announcement follows news releases the company issued on October 6 and October 20, 2026. item.title: Washington's China chip curbs put SK Hynix's $45-billion New York plant in doubt
item.description: SK Hynix wants to fund the Marcy, New York NAND plants with profits from an expanded China plant Commerce officials have not approved.
item.content:encoded: SK Hynix's American subsidiary, Solidigm, plans to invest approximately $45 billion to build two NAND flash memory plants in Marcy, New York, with the long-term investment potentially reaching $100 billion, according to a Reuters report. NAND is a type of flash memory used to store data persistently in devices including data centres. The company intends to fund the U.S. project using profits generated by expanding its existing chipmaking plant in Dalian, China. Solidigm has requested U.S. export licences for American-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment needed to expand the Dalian facility, but the Commerce Department has not yet approved them, Reuters reported. Solidigm executives have met with Commerce Department officials nearly 10 times since late August, most recently last week. Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler maintained in that meeting that additional American chipmaking tools for capacity expansion or facility upgrades at Dalian cannot be permitted, according to the report. The report said the Commerce Department has not formally rejected a licence for equipment destined for empty cleanroom space at Dalian, and that separate negotiations are continuing over 2027 equipment-maintenance licences. item.title: Novacap-led group buys NATO navigation supplier OSI Maritime, terms undisclosed

item.content:encoded: A consortium led by Montreal-based private equity firm Novacap, alongside Crown corporations Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada, has acquired OSI Maritime Systems, a Burnaby, B.C. company. The company is also developing what it calls an autonomy centre of excellence to support its work with the Royal Canadian Navy, through which it has previously developed products, OSI said. item.title: Falcon Energy Materials agrees to pay US$22 million for a Chinese graphite stake
item.description: The deal gives the TSX Venture-listed company a 49% stake in a profitable anode-material producer in Shandong province, funded by a private placement closed in September.
item.content:encoded: Falcon Energy Materials plc (TSX-V: FLCN; OTCQB: FLCNF) has agreed to acquire a 49% strategic, non-operating equity interest in Weihai Hensen New Materials Technology Co., Ltd., a Chinese producer of natural flake graphite and synthetic graphite anode materials, for US$22 million in cash. The transaction is being carried out through Falcon EMG Holdings Ltd, a wholly owned Falcon subsidiary, under an Equity Transfer Agreement with Weihai's sole equity holder. Weihai is based in Shandong province and operates a production facility with capacity for 25,000 tonnes a year of coated spheronized purified graphite, or CSPG, a processed anode material. Founded in 2023, the company began commercial production in the second half of 2025. Falcon's announcement describes Weihai as profitable, selling its output under long-term contracts to leading Chinese anode material manufacturers. Falcon describes the acquisition as a step in its strategy to become, in its own words, 'an integrated, global supplier of critical battery materials.' The 49% stake is structured as non-operating, so Falcon will not run Weihai's daily operations, but a shareholder agreement gives Falcon the right to nominate a director, a requirement that key decisions receive unanimous board approval, and rights of first offer and first refusal over Weihai's remaining equity. Falcon said the purchase is fully funded from a C$34-million non-brokered private placement that it closed on September 23, 2026. A non-brokered placement is one sold directly to investors without an underwriting syndicate acting as agent. The acquisition itself is expected to close by the end of the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to Chinese regulatory approvals, including registrations with the State Administration for Market Regulation and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, as well as other customary closing conditions. Falcon chief executive Matthieu Bos said the acquisition is 'a defining milestone for Falcon,' calling it the execution of commitments the company had previously made to its shareholders regarding its battery-materials strategy. Falcon's shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol FLCN and on the OTCQB marketplace under FLCNF.

item.title: Salesforce agrees to buy voice-AI startup Cresta in a deal reported at $2.7 billion

item.content:encoded: Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, an artificial intelligence company whose voice agents handle customer service calls end-to-end and coach human representatives in real time. Cresta already serves enterprise clients including Marriott, Comcast and Alaska Airlines. The acquisition is intended to pair Cresta's voice technology with Salesforce's Service Cloud and Agentforce products, extending the company's customer-service push from text and chat into phone calls. Kishan Chetan, who leads Agentforce and Service Cloud for Salesforce, said in the announcement that voice is 'where service is hardest to get right, and where it matters most to customers.' Cresta chief executive Ping Wu said the combination will help 'turn every customer interaction into a competitive advantage' by building real-time conversation intelligence directly into Salesforce's service platform. Salesforce said Cresta will continue to support the contact-centre and telephony platforms its customers currently use after the deal closes. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of Salesforce's 2028 fiscal year, subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions, the companies said. Neither company's announcement discloses the terms of the transaction beyond the expected timing, and the $2.7-billion figure circulating in media reports has not been confirmed by either party. item.title: Standard Uranium boosts its flow-through placement to $2 million
item.description: Strong demand led the Saskatchewan-focused explorer to increase the non-brokered offering to 25 million units at $0.08, with warrants exercisable at $0.12.
item.content:encoded: Standard Uranium Ltd. (TSXV: STND, OTCQB: STTDF) has increased the size of a previously announced private placement, citing strong investor demand. The non-brokered offering, conducted under the listed issuer financing exemption in National Instrument 45-106, will now raise up to $2 million through the sale of as many as 25 million flow-through units priced at $0.08 each. Each flow-through unit consists of one common share, issued under the flow-through provisions of the Income Tax Act, and one half of a common share purchase warrant. A whole warrant entitles its holder to buy one additional common share at $0.12, with the right to exercise beginning 61 days after closing and running until 24 months after that date. A flow-through share lets the issuer renounce the associated tax deductions to the subscriber rather than claiming them itself, which is why flow-through financings are priced at a premium and used specifically to fund Canadian exploration spending. Standard Uranium said the net proceeds from this offering will go toward exploring its Saskatchewan uranium projects. The release states the securities issued will not be subject to a resale hold period under applicable Canadian securities laws. Completion remains subject to acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, and finder's fees are payable to eligible parties who introduce subscribers to the offering, though no rate or specific finder is named. The release does not give a closing date for the offering, and it does not state the size of the previously announced placement that this increase replaces, so the scale of today's upsizing cannot be measured against the original offer. Standard Uranium has not named a specific lead or sole finder in the release.

item.title: A SpaceX-Tesla merger could hand Musk 56% voting control
item.description: Barclays estimates the combination would give Musk roughly 37% ownership of the combined company, without triggering the $1-trillion Tesla pay package shareholders approved.
item.content:encoded: A merger between SpaceX and Tesla could hand Elon Musk substantially more control over the combined company than the $1-trillion pay package Tesla shareholders approved last year, Reuters reported. Barclays analysts estimate that in a merger, Musk would own roughly 37% of the combined entity but hold about 56% of its voting power, a figure well above the roughly 29% voting control the Tesla package alone would eventually give him if every milestone is met. The difference comes from how the two pay structures are built. Tesla's package requires Musk to hit a series of market-capitalization and operational milestones before any additional stock, and the voting power that comes with it, is released. SpaceX's own compensation plan, approved separately, gives Musk 85% voting control from the outset, with no operational conditions attached, because of a special class of shares that carries ten votes each. SpaceX's stock-based incentives are themselves tied to ambitious targets — Mars colonization, data-center expansion, and further market-capitalization goals — that could be worth as much as $719 billion at the highest tier, according to the reporting. Under a merger scenario, any additional Tesla-linked award would not trigger until the combined company's market capitalization reached $2 trillion, versus Tesla's current standalone valuation of about $1.6 trillion; reaching that threshold would issue Musk $20 billion in shares. Governance observers quoted in the reporting were skeptical that the pay structure itself was the real story. Corporate governance expert Charles Elson called the package "a distraction from the real story, which is complete control." Accounting professor Matthew Bloomfield described the SpaceX plan as "just a marketing document," saying Musk includes ambitious targets to "get a bunch of people hyped." SpaceX completed its initial public offering in the summer of 2026, and the merger itself remains speculative — there is no confirmed transaction, only analysis of what one could look like under the two companies' existing pay structures. The $1-trillion Tesla package approved by shareholders last year was structured around milestones Musk had not yet met at the time of the reporting. item.title: A British Columbia regulator halted A.C.L. Construction's stock over late filings
item.description: The Fort St. John construction company's shares have been halted since October 6 while it refiles two years of financial statements under a corrected revenue method.
item.content:encoded: A.C.L. Construction Ltd. (TSXV: ACL, OTCQB: AACLF, FSE: A3L0) said November 1 that it has filed audited annual financial statements for the year ended May 31, 2026, along with restated comparative financial statements for the two years before it, and interim financial statements for the three months ended August 31, 2026. The restatement corrects how the Fort St. John, British Columbia-based company recognized revenue on its fixed-price construction contracts. The British Columbia Securities Commission issued a cease-trade order on October 5 because the company had not filed its annual financial statements, annual MD&A and related certifications by the September 28 deadline. Trading in A.C.L.'s shares was suspended on the TSX Venture Exchange on October 6 and remains halted; the company said it intends to apply to have the order revoked and trading reinstated, without giving a timeline. The company said it discovered the issue while preparing its annual financial statements, in consultation with its audit committee and auditor, MNP LLP. Its previous method recognized revenue on fixed-price construction contracts based on amounts invoiced to customers, which the company said did not meet the requirements of IFRS 15. It has replaced that method with one based on costs incurred to date relative to total estimated contract costs. For the year ended May 31, 2025, the restated figures raised reported revenue to $18,254,032 from $17,675,792 and narrowed the net and comprehensive loss to $693,820 from $1,203,987. The company's shareholders' deficit for that year grew to $191,649 from $163,732 under the restatement, a result of the same change in how revenue on fixed-price contracts is recognized. For the year before, ended May 31, 2024, the same change moved the figures in the other direction: revenue was restated down to $13,005,353 from $13,742,455, and the net loss widened to $1,066,455 from $528,371. The company attributed both changes to the switch from an invoicing-based to a cost-incurred-based revenue recognition method. The company also filed interim financial statements for the three months ended August 31, 2026, though the November 1 release gives no comparable figures for that quarter. It said it consulted its audit committee and auditor, MNP LLP, in identifying and correcting the revenue-recognition error, and that it intends to apply for revocation of the cease-trade order and reinstatement of trading, without specifying when.

item.title: A second suspected cyberattack pushed European supermarket fridges to 50 degrees
item.description: Refrigeration units in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden and Estonia spiked in temperature overnight.
item.content:encoded: Refrigeration and freezer systems in supermarkets across Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden and Estonia reported sudden temperature spikes overnight into Monday, with some units switching into defrost mode and others climbing toward 50 degrees Celsius. Ahold Delhaize stores and Colruyt-operated Spar locations were affected in Belgium and Luxembourg; ICA, including its Baronen store in Stockholm, and six Coop stores reported the same in Sweden, and one unnamed chain was affected in Estonia. Sabcobel chief executive Stephan Moelans said the incident "was a cyberattack"; an ICA store separately said its units had been "hacked." Other reports described the episode only as a suspected attack or an IT incident. One store reported the intrusion at around 2 a.m. and discovered it at 5:30 a.m., according to the reporting. It follows a cyberattack last month in France that pushed hundreds of supermarket cooling units to 50 degrees Celsius, causing fires and spoiled food, and a separate cybersecurity incident that Ahold Delhaize reported to Dutch police the same month. Kitman Coldtech, a refrigeration technology supplier, was also named in connection with the incident. item.title: Binance says customers pulled $4.7 billion after its $6.3 billion hack
item.description: The exchange reopened withdrawals after a 48-hour freeze following the theft, which the FBI has linked to the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.
item.content:encoded: Binance said Monday that customers had withdrawn a net $4.72 billion from the exchange since it reopened withdrawals on Sunday morning. The company had frozen withdrawals for roughly 48 hours after disclosing a $6.3 billion theft, which it has called potentially the largest financial heist in history. The exchange reported $2.7 billion of inflows after reopening, and said withdrawal volumes had since declined and stabilized. The Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a hacking group the agency links to North Korea. Binance co-chief executive Yi He said the exchange's "top priority right now is to ensure the environment is secure, after which users can withdraw their funds." Binance said it is covering customer losses with company funds, having already raised $6 billion from its corporate treasury, an insurance fund and reserves set aside for security breaches. The stablecoin issuer Circle said it had frozen more than $1.1 billion in USDC tied to the theft. Bitcoin, which had fallen to a six-week low after the hack became public, had recovered to around $78,000 by Monday. Spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $643 million of outflows the Friday before Binance reopened withdrawals, and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in the aftermath of the hack, according to the reporting. North Korea-linked hackers have stolen a combined $7.4 billion from crypto platforms in 2026. item.title: China's robot makers are racing to build AI 'brains', not just bodies
item.description: Chinese embodied-AI startups raised about $13 billion in the first half of 2026, five times the prior year, as the industry shifts focus from humanoid stunts to software.
item.content:encoded: Chinese robotics companies that spent years building humanoids capable of running, dancing and performing backflips are now shifting resources into the software that could make those machines useful across a wider range of jobs, Reuters reported from Beijing. Chinese embodied-AI companies raised 93.5 billion yuan, or about $13 billion, across 322 deals in the first half of 2026 — five times the amount raised a year earlier, according to the research firm ITjuzi. Spirit AI co-founder Gao Yang said "the brain is indeed the weakest link in the complete robotics stack." Hangzhou-based Unitree, one of the world's largest humanoid robot makers by shipments, has about 30 researchers working on AI that predicts how objects behave. Ant Group's robotics unit, Robbyant, has trained a model on 160,000 hours of material, including 50,000 hours of human-guided robot movements, across 20 robot configurations from 17 different brands. DexForce, which trains robots in computer-generated environments, says it can prepare some industrial tasks for deployment within six to eight hours, with success rates above 99.9% in specified precision operations, according to chief operating officer Nicole Yang. The Chinese battery maker CATL said Spirit AI's robots achieved an insertion success rate above 99% connecting flexible wires during its battery-pack testing. American startups including Physical Intelligence, Skild AI and Generalist are pursuing a similar goal: software that lets a robot learn a new task without lengthy retraining. Three Chinese companies — X Square, Galaxea and Spirit AI — have each reached valuations of about $3 billion, and Hong Kong-listed UBTech advertised a chief scientist role paying up to 124 million yuan, or about $18 million, including equity and benefits. Shanghai-based ZenGen Labs founder Dermot McGrath concluded that the profit margin in robotics will come from the software rather than the hardware, according to the reporting. Unitree founder Wang Xingxing said a future version of the underlying AI models could bring robotics its own "ChatGPT moment" if robots can complete most tasks in unfamiliar environments from spoken instructions alone. item.title: Russian strikes knock out power for hundreds of thousands in Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian drones struck a Russian missile plant in Rostov and caused significant damage in Nizhny Novgorod the same night, as a local ceasefire held elsewhere.
item.content:encoded: Russian missile and drone strikes hit power infrastructure across four Ukrainian regions overnight into Sunday, leaving hundreds of thousands of households without electricity, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's air force said it shot down 371 of 433 long-range Russian drones launched since Saturday evening, according to Reuters, which did not specify how many struck their targets. Ukraine struck back at targets inside Russia. Drones hit the Kamensky plant in Russia's Rostov region, which Ukraine says is involved in missile manufacturing, Reuters reported. Nizhny Novgorod governor Gleb Nikitin said a separate, large-scale drone attack caused significant damage to an industrial facility in his region, which is home to the NORSI oil refinery, one of Russia's largest. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 235 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight. A six-day local ceasefire around the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky held through its final day, Reuters reported, even as fighting continued elsewhere along the front line and both sides kept up long-range strikes. Ukraine says it supports a broader ceasefire specifically covering energy-infrastructure targets, and says Russia has not agreed to one. US President Donald Trump has asked Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries, Reuters reported, saying such strikes have helped push up diesel prices ahead of US midterm elections. On the venture boards, CM Bulletin's defence-and-drones theme — eight listed names tied to the sector by their registered name or sector label — was mixed on the day the strikes were reported. Five of the eight traded; none rose and three fell, for a median move of -2.07%, against a -2.77% decline for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. Aegis Critical Energy Defence Corp. (CSE:QESS) fell 11.11% to C$0.24, qualifying for the theme because its registered name contains "defence." Alchemy Labs Inc (TSXV:ALCH) fell 9.88% to C$0.73, in the theme because its sector label is "Aerospace & Defense." Kraken Robotics Inc (TSXV:PNG) fell 2.07% to C$3.78, its registered name being Kraken Robotics Inc. The declines fall on the same day as the strikes reported above. Neither the reporting on the strikes nor the quotes behind these moves draws any connection between the two, and none is implied here.

item.title: Eureka Metals wants $499,134 from shareholders at a penny a share
item.description: The rights offering precedes a proposed share consolidation of up to six-for-one, with rights expiring December 1.
item.content:encoded: Eureka Metals Corp. (CSE: ERKA) (OTCQB: UREKF) (FSE: S580), a Canadian mineral explorer holding titanium, vanadium, scandium and other polymetallic projects in Quebec and British Columbia, has launched a rights offering to raise up to $499,134. Holders of common shares as of November 6, 2026 will receive one transferable right for each share held. Each right entitles its holder to subscribe for one pre-consolidation common share at $0.01. Rights expire December 1, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Toronto time, and the company expects the offering to close on or about December 2, 2026. Odyssey Trust Company is acting as rights agent. Eureka separately proposes to consolidate its shares on a basis of up to six pre-consolidation shares for every one post-consolidation share, with the final ratio to be set by the board. The company had 49,913,367 shares outstanding before the offering; if every right is exercised, that would roughly double to about 99,826,734 shares before the consolidation is applied. At the maximum six-for-one ratio and full exercise of the rights, Eureka would have approximately 16,637,789 shares outstanding following both the offering and the consolidation. The company says the consolidation remains subject to Canadian Securities Exchange approval, and shares are expected to continue trading under the ticker ERKA. The company said net proceeds from the rights offering, combined with its existing working capital, are expected to fund exploration and property costs, general and administrative expenses, and unallocated working capital. The offering is open to shareholders in all Canadian provinces and territories and in select international jurisdictions, excluding the United States. The release does not state whether the dollar figures in the offering are Canadian or U.S. currency. Eureka is a Canadian company listed primarily on the Canadian Securities Exchange, with secondary listings on the OTCQB in the United States and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

item.title: First Atlantic buys a Newfoundland property never tested for hydrogen
item.description: The explorer is paying 1,000,000 shares for 209 claims in the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex, where nearby ground shows historic chromite finds.
item.content:encoded: First Atlantic Nickel & Cobalt Corp. (TSXV: FAN) (OTCQB: FANCF) (FSE: P210) has signed an agreement, dated October 30, 2026, to acquire 100% of the North Arm Ophiolite Property on Newfoundland's west coast from two arm's-length vendors. The company will pay with 1,000,000 common shares issued at a deemed price of $0.55 each and will reimburse $51,250 in refundable security deposits the vendors had posted with the government of Newfoundland and Labrador. The property comprises three mineral licences totalling 209 claim cells across 52.25 square kilometres on the north shore of North Arm, within the Bay of Islands Ophiolite Complex. It lies about 25 kilometres north of First Atlantic's existing Ophiolite-X project. The company says the ground has seen limited modern exploration and has never been systematically tested for geologic hydrogen or for awaruite, a naturally occurring nickel-iron-cobalt alloy. First Atlantic points to historic chromite occurrences at nearby Blow Me Down and Springers Hill, and to active hydrogen-bearing alkaline springs at the nearby Tablelands, which the company says demonstrate ongoing serpentinization. The property itself carries no underlying royalty or option payments to a third party. Closing is conditional on TSX Venture Exchange acceptance and is expected about five business days afterward, by January 31, 2027. The 1,000,000 payment shares will be subject to a four-month-and-one-day hold period from issuance, the standard resale restriction attached to shares issued outside a prospectus offering. The company also granted 950,000 incentive stock options to directors and to an investor-relations consultant, exercisable at $0.55 per share for five years. The consultant's options vest quarterly over twelve months; the release does not state vesting terms for the options granted to directors. First Atlantic's existing project in the region, Pipestone XL, spans a 30-kilometre stretch of ophiolite complex and includes awaruite deposits the company says carry about 77% nickel content along with secondary chromium mineralization, according to the company's own description of its business.

item.title: Binance resumes bitcoin withdrawals after replacing $6 billion in stolen crypto
item.description: The exchange covered roughly 95% of October's $6.3 billion hack, which the FBI has tied to a North Korean hacking unit.
item.content:encoded: Binance began resuming withdrawals in phases on Sunday, starting with bitcoin shortly after 0600 GMT and followed within hours by ether, BNB, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens, after the exchange said it had covered roughly 95%, or about $6 billion, of the $6.3 billion in crypto stolen in October. The remaining 5%, in less liquid assets, is still being sourced, Binance said. The FBI said it had tied the theft to a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit it calls TraderTraitor, which the bureau said laundered the stolen assets by converting them into Ethereum. Asked about the attribution, President Trump said: "We don't know if it's North Korea — but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it." Binance funded the replacement tokens using half of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users, along with portions of its futures insurance fund and corporate treasury, the exchange said. Co-chief executive Yi He said the company was committed to replenishing the Secure Asset Fund back to about $1 billion. Founder Changpeng Zhao thanked law enforcement for its help, saying "a tweet can't fully express our gratitude." Binance, described in the report as the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said the phased restart ultimately covered 15 crypto assets, beginning with bitcoin and followed by ether, BNB, XRP, dogecoin and the USDT and USDC stablecoins, restoring withdrawal access across the tokens affected by the October halt. The theme of digital-asset names on Canada's venture boards comprises 14 listed companies; five traded today, one higher and four lower, for a median move of -4.88% against -2.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of -2.11 percentage points on the day Binance announced the restored withdrawals. Neptune Digital Assets Corp (TSXV: NDA) fell 5.88% to $0.48, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "digital asset." Dmg Blockchain Solutions Inc (TSXV: DMGI) fell 4.88% to $0.39, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "blockchain." The moves and the Binance news fall on the same day; nothing here connects the two.

item.title: New Break seeks $550,000 to fund drilling at its Timmins-area gold project
item.description: The flow-through financing would fund exploration spending at the company's Moray project, 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, if it closes as planned.
item.content:encoded: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK) said October 30 that it intends to complete a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,500,000 flow-through common shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of up to $550,000. The company expects the offering to close within the next two business days, subject to acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange and other customary conditions. The shares qualify as flow-through shares within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). New Break said the proceeds will be used for Canadian Exploration Expenses, which it will renounce to the purchasers of the shares with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, as stated in the release. The company said the proceeds raised through the offering will go toward ongoing drilling at its Moray gold project, located 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, in the Abitibi greenstone belt. The release gave no drill results or further technical detail on the current program. Qualified finders who introduce subscribers to the offering may receive a cash fee equal to 6% of the proceeds from those subscribers, plus finder's warrants equal to 6% of the flow-through shares sold to them, exercisable at $0.22 per share for 24 months from closing, according to the release. All securities issued under the offering, including any finder's warrants, are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, the standard resale restriction under Canadian securities law for this type of exemption. New Break describes itself as a Canadian mineral exploration company focused primarily on the Moray project, and also holds a 20% carried interest in the Sundog gold project in Nunavut. The release did not disclose the size of New Break's partner's interest in Sundog or any other terms of that arrangement.

item.title: A Southeast Asian conglomerate still awaits one approval for Altura's $3-million raise
item.description: Altura Energy extended the deadline to close its $3-million helium financing to November 30 while its investor's bank sign-off is pending.
item.content:encoded: Altura Energy Corp. (TSXV: ALTU) said October 30 that it has extended, to November 30, 2026, the deadline to complete a non-brokered private placement of 18,541,400 units at $0.1618 each, for gross proceeds of C$3 million. The TSX Venture Exchange has granted conditional acceptance of the offering, which the company first disclosed in a July 28, 2026 news release. Each unit under the offering comprises one common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.25 for 36 months from the closing date. A non-brokered placement is one an issuer sells directly to subscribers rather than through an investment dealer, which is consistent with the release naming no agent or underwriter on the transaction. The sole subscriber is described in the release only as a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate; Altura's release does not name the investor. That investor has obtained approval from its own local Ministry of Finance to proceed, but the release said it is still awaiting a further approval from its state bank before the financing can close. Altura said the investor will have the right to nominate one member to the board of directors once the placement completes; the release did not disclose who might be nominated or any further governance terms attached to the investment beyond that right. The extension is the only change disclosed in the October 30 release; the unit count, the per-unit price and the warrant terms are unchanged from the July 28 announcement, according to the company. No new closing date beyond November 30, 2026, was given, and the release did not say what happens if that date passes without the state bank's approval. Altura describes itself as a helium-focused exploration company advancing prospects in the Holbrook Basin of Arizona, targeting helium for uses the company lists as healthcare, semiconductors, aerospace and other advanced-technology applications. The company also trades on the OTCQB under the symbol ALTUF and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under Y020.

item.title: Edgewater Wireless settles debenture interest in shares, including some to its own directors
item.description: The TSX Venture company will issue 1,421,982 shares at $0.05 to cover $71,100 in interest owed on debentures issued in 2022.
item.content:encoded: Edgewater Wireless Systems Inc. (TSXV: YFI) said October 30 that it will settle an aggregate of $71,100.01 owed in interest on its unsecured debentures, issued September 1, 2022, by issuing 1,421,982 common shares at a deemed price of $0.05 per share. The interest covers four quarterly obligations dated December 1, 2025, March 1, 2026, June 1, 2026 and September 1, 2026. Of the shares being issued, 265,995 are going to company directors, the release said. Edgewater said that participation triggers the related-party transaction requirements of Multilateral Instrument 61-101, which governs transactions between an issuer and its insiders. Edgewater said it qualifies for an exemption from the formal-valuation and minority-shareholder-approval requirements that would otherwise apply, because neither the fair value of the shares nor the debt being settled exceeds 25% of the company's market capitalization, as calculated under the instrument. The debt settlement remains subject to the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange, the company said. The release did not state when that approval is expected or what happens to the arrangement if it is not granted. Separately, Edgewater said it granted 900,000 stock options to employees and consultants at an exercise price of $0.05 per share. The options expire five years from the date of grant, according to the release. Edgewater also trades over the counter in the United States under the symbol KPIFF. The release gave no further detail on the company's current financial position or on why the interest was settled in shares rather than cash.

item.title: OpenAI cuts its funding target by $10 billion as AI stocks slide
item.description: The ChatGPT maker now seeks $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from a $30 billion target.
item.content:encoded: OpenAI has cut the target for its latest funding round by $10 billion, now seeking about $20 billion rather than the $30 billion it had been pursuing, according to a Financial Times report carried by Reuters. The company is also seeking a lower valuation, $1.25 trillion rather than the $1.4 trillion target. OpenAI had set a Friday deadline for investor commitments, Reuters reported. The reduction follows a selloff across technology stocks tied to concerns over the scale of AI infrastructure spending. Reuters reported the Nasdaq fell 2.9% on the day the cut was reported and is down 7.8% from its October 6 peak. Some investors have reduced the size of their commitments to the round, and the fund's 'first close' — the initial tranche of capital committed — is expected to come in below the revised $20 billion target. Reuters named several participants in the round, including the UAE-backed technology fund MGX, expected to be the largest investor, alongside Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz. OpenAI is pursuing a public listing in 2027, and Reuters reported the company had been keen to close this round ahead of rival Anthropic's anticipated listing, since the two companies draw on an overlapping investor base. The theme comprises 29 listed venture names; 18 traded today, 5 higher and 9 lower, for a median move of -2.17% against -2.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. The spread between the two was 0.60 percentage points. Perimeter Medical Imaging Ai In (TSXV: PINK) rose 28.57% to CAD0.18, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) fell 8.77% to CAD2.08, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." Railtown AI Technologies Inc (CSE: RAIL) rose 1.72% to CAD0.295, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." OpenAI's funding news and these moves fell on the same trading day. Nothing in the public record ties the two together: the theme's -2.17% median move and the Composite's -2.77% decline are both simply what the board did that day.

item.title: Ashley Gold closes C$2.08-million private placement in two tranches
item.description: The final tranche raised C$631,275 at 6.5 and 8 cents a unit, pending Canadian Securities Exchange acceptance of the full offering.
item.content:encoded: Ashley Gold Corp., a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on gold and polymetallic deposits, has closed the second and final tranche of a non-brokered private placement. The tranche raised additional gross proceeds of C$631,275, taking the offering's aggregate gross proceeds, combined with a first tranche that closed October 19, 2026, to C$2,077,461.49. The release states the offering remains subject to final acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. The final tranche was split between two unit types. The company issued 6,635,000 non-flow-through units at C$0.065 per unit, for gross proceeds of C$431,275, and 2,500,000 flow-through units at C$0.08 per unit, for gross proceeds of C$200,000. Flow-through units carry tax deductions the company renounces to the subscriber; non-flow-through units do not. Each non-flow-through unit consists of one common share and one-half of a warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at C$0.12 for 24 months. Each flow-through unit consists of one flow-through common share and one-half of a warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at C$0.15 for 24 months. The company paid aggregate cash finder's fees of C$45,042 and issued 652,800 non-transferable finder warrants, exercisable between C$0.065 and C$0.08, in connection with the offering. All securities issued in the final tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 1, 2027. Net proceeds from the flow-through portion are earmarked for eligible Canadian exploration expenses that qualify as flow-through mining expenditures, which the company will renounce to subscribers effective December 31, 2026. Chief executive Darcy Christian called the financing the largest in the company's history, citing continued support from new and returning investors. Following the close, the company had 129,888,470 common shares outstanding. The release describes the company's flagship assets as 100%-owned claims in the Dryden area of Ontario, plus an optioned Icefield claim package in British Columbia.

item.title: Goliath Resources raises C$9.8 million without issuing a single warrant
item.description: The non-brokered flow-through placement, still subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval, funds exploration at the Golddigger-Surebet gold project in BC's Golden Triangle.
item.content:encoded: Goliath Resources Limited, an explorer of precious-metals projects in the Golden Triangle of northwestern British Columbia, has closed a non-brokered private placement for gross proceeds of C$9,800,000. The company issued 6,057,000 flow-through common shares at a price of C$1.62 per share. No warrants were attached to the units, and the company paid no finder's fees or commissions in connection with the offering. The shares were issued as flow-through shares, which qualify under subsection 66(15) of Canada's Income Tax Act. That designation lets the company renounce the associated tax deductions for qualifying exploration expenditures to the subscribers who bought the shares, rather than claiming those deductions itself — a structure used to attract investors to exploration-stage mining financings. Goliath said the funds will go toward Canadian exploration expenses and flow-through mining expenditures on its Golddigger-Surebet Gold Project. The qualifying expenditures must be incurred by December 31, 2027, and the associated tax deductions renounced to subscribers by December 31, 2026. The offering remains subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, the release states. The shares issued are subject to a statutory four-month hold period expiring March 1, 2027, under applicable Canadian securities law. Chief executive Roger Rosmus said the financing is "an insurance policy that further enhances our strong balance sheet and puts us in a stronger position, with ~C$27.5M in cash going into 2027 and our planned exploration drill program." The company describes its projects as sitting in "high quality geological settings and geopolitical safe jurisdictions amenable to mining in Canada." In 2026 it completed a fully funded 48,443-metre drill program on the Golddigger-Surebet project, for which assays are pending on 55 holes, following a 64,364-metre program in 2025.
